extracted.intended_audience: Congressional policymakers, federal agency designers, university and medical school administrators, and leaders of the medical research community
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and recommended standards for establishing and operating an independent federal agency to support medical research, including principles of administration, composition, funding mechanisms, and oversight. Covers criteria for grants, fellowships, institutional block grants, governance, and protections against political influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency flexibility and experimental authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Until experience has indicated the best plan of organization and procedure, the Federal agency created to aid medical research should be kept as flexible as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority to experiment with organization should be written into the agency's charter to avoid ossification and loss of purpose: 'Only if authority to experiment with organization is written into its charter will an agency designed to aid medical research escape this fate.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from political influence
rubrics_metrics.description: The administration of Federal aid to medical research must be free from political influence and protected against special pressures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency's structure and practices should guard against political or special-interest pressure affecting funding decisions or policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-experienced administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Men who are experienced in research and who understand the problems of the investigator should administer the agency and determine its policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the agency will focus on basic scientific research and training in civilian institutions, it should not be dominated by existing governmental services with specialized interests (e.g., armed forces, Public Health Service).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid domination or regimentation of research
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency should not attempt to dominate or regiment medical research but should function by creating greater opportunities and more freedom for investigation and by aiding in cooperative efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It should not attempt to influence selection of personnel, conditions of tenure, salary levels, or other internal affairs of recipient institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modest, conservative funding growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Any program of Federal aid to medical research should be modestly initiated in terms of actual needs and conservatively increased as the capacity of the medical schools to utilize additional funds is demonstrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid spending so much that other sources (philanthropy, industry) are driven out; preserve schools' freedom to pursue other donors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint on lifetime chairs and prolonged fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: The establishment of life-time research professorships, or of protracted research fellowships, at the expense of Federal funds is considered unwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In exceptional instances (unusual ability or need to free a senior person for research) support should come from general research funds or grants-in-aid rather than permanent federal endowments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against lowering research quality
rubrics_metrics.description: A grave danger in any effort to accelerate discovery is the ease with which the quality of the work can be lowered by encouraging men to undertake research who are inadequately prepared or unfitted for the task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constantly encourage confirmatory work and 'challenging investigations' to guard against mediocre or dangerous research that could mislead medical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a broad view beyond fund disbursement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency should not serve merely as a mechanism for disbursing funds for particular research projects, but should always attempt to maintain a broad view of the needs of the whole field of medical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency activities should include coordination, assessment of field-wide needs, and initiation of essential new work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid awarding prizes or appearing as scientific authority
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be unwise for a national body concerned with medical research to give prizes or otherwise to dispense praise or blame; the agency should avoid even the semblance of scientific authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What is acceptable in medicine must be established by tested methods of examination, not by the imprimatur of a national body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage individual initiative and avoid coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency should come to share in the leadership of medical investigation by encouraging individual initiative and freedom of research, with a careful avoidance of coercion and regimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote scientific curiosity and cooperation rather than centralized control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an independent agency (de novo)
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical research could best be promoted by the creation of an independent Federal agency, to be created de novo and independent of all existing agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new body should supplement existing agencies, not conflict with them; independence is required because existing agencies have specialized interests and cannot fairly sponsor a broad civilian-oriented research program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of trustees composition and appointment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The board of trustees is to consist of five persons appointed without regard to the Civil Service Laws by the President and subject to Senate confirmation, chosen on the basis of scientific achievement and leadership, wide knowledge of medical problems, capacity for administration and organization, and with reasonable regard for geographical representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board elects own chairman; members serve part-time for 5 years, not eligible for reappointment (with limited exceptions); no two members may be from the same institution; original members staggered (2–6 years) to assure continuity and rotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of trustees duties and meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: The board of trustees is to determine the broad policies of the Foundation, appoint members of the technical board, approve or disapprove technical board recommendations, and establish liaison offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board to meet not less than once each month and hold at least one regular meeting annually in each major geographical area; chairman represents Foundation in interagency matters; liaison officers may attend deliberations without vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration for trustees
rubrics_metrics.description: Each member of the board of trustees is to be paid a salary of seventy-five hundred dollars ($7,500) per annum for that portion of his time which he devotes to the services of the Foundation, and receive travel expenses and per diem as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensation is intended to encourage committed service and to offset potential loss of outside income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical board composition and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: A technical board, composed initially of 12 persons, is to be appointed by the board of trustees and chosen on the basis of knowledge and experience in special fields of medical research and related sciences, with reasonable geographical representation; members remain in their parent institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership terms are staggered; members serve part-time (3 years), are generally not eligible for reappointment, and no two members should be from the same institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and functions of the technical board
rubrics_metrics.description: The technical board is to receive, review and recommend to the board of trustees on all requests for general research funds, fellowships, and grants-in-aid; to put approved programs into effect; maintain reasonable supervision of work and Fellows; and prepare reports as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized to convene round-table discussions, invite summaries of specific problems, seek authoritative information, and receive recommendations from individual investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of aides and ad hoc committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Each technical board member may appoint one or more aides (part-time up to 3 years) selected on basis of qualification; technical board to appoint ad hoc committees as needed, with consultants receiving per diem up to $25 and travel expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure aides remain professionally active and that service does not jeopardize academic careers; aides and committees discharged on member term expiration unless successor invites continuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive secretary and administrative staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: A full-time executive secretary is to be appointed by the board of trustees to organize administrative, fiscal, and accounting offices to conduct the Foundation's business; except for the executive secretary, staff to be drawn from civil-service lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiscal actions approved by trustees are implemented by the executive secretary and affiliated officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions of the Foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation's functions are to (a) further medical research by providing financial aid through general research funds, fellowships and grants-in-aid; (b) coordinate research in progress and initiate new essential work; (c) establish necessary liaison to secure a free exchange of medical information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial aid mechanisms should be designed to promote, coordinate, and disseminate medical research effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: General research funds — eligibility and administration
rubrics_metrics.description: On application, a block grant may be made to a medical school for general use over 1 to 10 years for the promotion of research provided the institution can present evidence that it can efficiently utilize the funds and is prepared to give reasonable accounting of expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution must have a research committee (preferably executive faculty and active investigators) responsible for administration, reports, and accounting; institutions allowed wide latitude but subject to periodic review and cancellation by the Foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralization and block grants to local research boards
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of funds as block grants to local research boards would exercise decentralization of control; eliminate costly overhead; create a flexible mechanism to meet rapidly varying needs; and allow local faculties to exercise judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local boards are best placed to select junior fellows and meet small, rapidly changing needs; central agencies lack flexibility for numerous small items and local knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of general research funds for junior fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: General research funds should be used in part to provide 'junior fellowships' allowing medical students to interrupt their course and devote 1–2 years full-time to research; junior fellowships are not to be used as scholarships to defray medical school tuition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates for these fellowships will be unknown to a central agency and selection should be made by the local research board; Foundation to review institutional policies on number and stipend value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal renewal timing and appeals for general funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal discussions concerning renewal of general research funds should be completed 1 to 3 years in advance of termination; if an application is refused, the applicant institution may appeal directly to the board of trustees for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In allocation, the Foundation should consider immediate needs, promise of institutional development, and effects on parent institution support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowships — purpose, duration, and selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are to be awarded for 1 to 3 years to approved applicants (M.D., Ph.D., D.D.S., or equivalent) to acquire research training, undertake research, learn special techniques, or pursue related studies; initial selection should weigh potential for leadership as heavily as past performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships are primarily for research training, not residencies or primarily for postgraduate degrees or specialty certification; should include teaching or clinical experience; stipends set with reference to university salaries and to encourage senior men; research expenses and insurance/annuity matching may be supported; fellowship lapses on unauthorized transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants-in-aid — scope, endorsements, and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants-in-aid, extending for 1 to 10 years, may be made to universities, medical schools, or nonprofit scientific institutions for support of specific projects or specified investigators; applications must carry endorsement of the applicant institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal renewal discussions should be completed prior to the last third of the grant period; reasonable overhead may be included but is not automatic; reports required; equipment purchased becomes property of the recipient institution; refusals may be appealed to the board of trustees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overhead and equipment ownership policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable overhead expenses may be included in requests for grants, but overhead payments are not automatic. Equipment purchased under general research funds or grants-in-aid is to become the property of the institution to which the funds are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundation retains review power over overhead; equipment ownership clarifies institutional responsibility and stewardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application for general research funds or grants-in-aid is refused, the applicant institution may appeal directly to the board of trustees for a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows an institutional review path beyond technical board decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection emphasis for initial Fellows
rubrics_metrics.description: In the initial selection of Fellows, potentialities for development of leadership in medicine should be weighed as heavily as past performance in research work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection policy should balance demonstrated achievement and future leadership potential to build long-term research capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on fellowship use
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are not to be used to provide residencies, or primarily for obtaining postgraduate degrees or for qualifying for Certification by the Specialty Boards; fellowships should include teaching or clinical care experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships are primarily intended to enable men to receive research training and engage in active research while ensuring balanced training relevant to medical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching of insurance/annuity-payments for Fellows
rubrics_metrics.description: If an institution matches insurance or annuity payments by its faculty, a similar payment is to be added by the Foundation to the Fellow’s stipend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundation should consider institutional practices in determining stipend packages to avoid penalizing fellows financially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship lapse on unauthorized transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: A fellowship is to lapse automatically if a Fellow transfers to another institution without approval by the Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures continuity of training and accountability for location and supervision of funded Fellows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of renewal discussions for grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal discussions concerning renewal of grants-in-aid should be completed prior to the beginning of the last third of the period of the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early planning avoids interruptions and allows timely review of progress and institutional capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of institutional development and parent support
rubrics_metrics.description: In allocating general research funds, the Foundation is to consider both the immediate needs and promise of development of the applicant institutions, and is to take cognizance of the effects of such funds upon the support of medical schools by their parent institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unintentionally displacing existing institutional support or creating perverse incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent policy for government-sponsored research
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent is granted on research which has been sponsored by Government in whole or in part, the ownership of the patent remain in the inventor, and the Government receive, in addition to a royalty-free license, the power to require the licensing of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach preserves inventor ownership while ensuring governmental ability to secure public benefit and prevent misuse; recognizes diversity of institutional patent practices.
